raw_response:
I will keep the wheat-maize double crop on all 8 mu. At my age, and with only part of the family available for field work, I do not want to gamble on an unfamiliar crop. Wheat and maize are what I know, and on this land they are still the safest way to keep grain output steady. I have enough experience to adjust the input rate a little, but I will not chase the highest possible yield. Fertilizer is expensive, and well irrigation also costs money, so I will put enough on to protect yield, then split it at the key stages instead of throwing everything at once. For wheat, I care most about a solid stand before winter and one good topdress at jointing. For maize, the turnaround after wheat is very tight, so I will keep land preparation simple and plant quickly with hybrid seed. If rainfall is normal, I will not over-irrigate maize, but if the field turns dry around jointing and grain filling, I will use the well. My thinking is simple: stable yield first, cash flow second, and no unnecessary risk.
